articles.title: Error Handling Patterns for Apache Kafka Applications
articles.read_scope: Complete article, Patterns 1–4 and Recovery; diagrams described in surrounding prose, no code executed.

practice.trigger: A failed event takes a slower retry path.
practice.failure: Later related events overtake it and change business outcomes.
practice.mechanism: Choose blocking, quarantine, or per-key ordered retry; recover routing state before resuming.
practice.conditions: Define the ordering key and preserve ownership across restart and rebalance.
practice.counterexample: Independent events need no shared ordering barrier.
practice.verification: Delay event A, deliver B for its key, crash the router, and inspect recovered effect order.

limitations: Architecture sketch omits a complete atomic commit and rebalance protocol.

articles.title: At-Least-Once Dead Lettering
articles.read_scope: Complete narrative, example, metrics, caveats, and best practices; commands inspected but not executed.

practice.trigger: Failed messages must survive transfer to quarantine.
practice.failure: Default dead lettering can lose messages while its target is unavailable.
practice.mechanism: Where supported, retain source messages until confirmed target acceptance; bound backlog.
practice.conditions: RabbitMQ quorum source with at-least-once policy, reject-publish overflow, and configured routing.
practice.counterexample: Loss-tolerant diagnostic messages may justify weaker transfer.
practice.verification: Disable target, cause dead lettering, restore target, and check duplicates, source retention, and pressure.

limitations: RabbitMQ 3.10 article; current documentation cross-check required.

articles.title: Infinite message deduplication in JetStream
articles.read_scope: Complete article including deletion/republication demonstration and indexing tradeoff; commands inspected but not executed.

practice.trigger: A producer restarts after an uncertain publish.
practice.failure: Its replay exceeds the broker duplicate window.
practice.mechanism: Use stable event identity and select a retention-backed deduplication contract.
practice.conditions: Per-subject rejection requires the prior key record to remain retained.
practice.counterexample: Deleting or expiring that record permits publication again; consumer effects remain separate.
practice.verification: Replay before and after expiry, then delete the record and repeat.

limitations: Publication deduplication is not external-effect atomicity; historical competitive claims are not adopted.

articles.title: Automated Worker Versioning with GitHub Actions
articles.read_scope: Complete technical walkthrough, rollout, rollback, pipeline and version identity; linked demo not executed.

practice.failure: Old execution loses compatible capacity or replays incompatible code.
practice.mechanism: Route by deployment version and retire old capacity only after drain evidence.
practice.conditions: Pinned work needs retained compatible workers; auto-upgrade requires replay-safe changes.
practice.counterexample: Rolling back new traffic does not move executions already pinned to a bad version.
practice.verification: Start old work, deploy twice, finish it, and exercise stuck-version recovery.

limitations: Example deployment is illustrative; SDK, server and controller versions constrain APIs.
